question.worked_solution:
We have a product of a positive number and a negative number, so the product will be negative:

$$
\frac{4}{3}\cdot (-\frac{9}{2})=-(\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{9}{2})
$$

Now, we multiply the fractions by multiplying the numerators and denominators separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}-(\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{9}{2}) & =-(\frac{4\cdot 9}{3\cdot 2}) \\  & =-(\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot 3}{3\cdot 2}) \\  & =-(\frac{2\cdot \cancel{2}\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}\cdot \cancel{2}}) \\  & =-(\frac{6}{1}) \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$
